method: OPEN AND QUOTED, from the 'Yellow fever' chapter of the Australian Immunisation Handbook, retrieved 2026-09-23. Every pass claim is machine re-checkable. LICENCE: Free to read but NOT openly licensed -- health.gov.au states 'all other rights are reserved'. Quoted with attribution on the same footing as the Stroke Foundation, Kidney Health Australia and NHFA/CSANZ sources already in this compendium.

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Yellow fever vaccination and the ICVP certificate are given only at state- or territory-approved Yellow Fever Vaccination Centres.**
claims.source_text: Yellow Fever Vaccination Centres can give yellow fever vaccinations and ICVPs. Relevant state or territory health authorities approve these centres.
claims.locator: Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing, 'Yellow fever', The Australian Immunisation Handbook, at https://immunisationhandbook.health.gov.au/contents/vaccine-preventable-diseases/yellow-fever, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **The certificate becomes valid 10 days after vaccination.** Arrivals without a valid ICVP are told to **seek medical assessment if symptoms develop within 6 days** of leaving a yellow fever-declared place.
claims.source_text: certificate becomes valid 10 days after vaccination. Travellers arriving in Australia who do not have a valid ICVP receive information about yellow fever. They are advised to promptly seek medical assessment if they develop relevant symptoms within 6 days of leaving a yellow fever-declared place.
claims.locator: Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing, 'Yellow fever', The Australian Immunisation Handbook, at https://immunisationhandbook.health.gov.au/contents/vaccine-preventable-diseases/yellow-fever, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Adults 60 and over have a higher risk of severe adverse events** — neurotropic and viscerotropic. **They should be vaccinated only if they intend to travel to endemic countries.**
claims.source_text: Adults aged ≥60 years have a higher risk of severe adverse events after yellow fever vaccination than younger adults. … Adults ≥60 years of age should receive yellow fever vaccine only if they intend to travel to endemic countries
claims.locator: Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing, 'Yellow fever', The Australian Immunisation Handbook, at https://immunisationhandbook.health.gov.au/contents/vaccine-preventable-diseases/yellow-fever, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **One dose gives lifelong immunity in most healthy adults and children** — protective antibody in **75–100% measured 10–69 years after vaccination**.
claims.source_text: lifelong immunity in most healthy adults and children. Protective levels of neutralising antibodies have been detected in 75-100% of healthy adults from endemic and non- endemic yellow fever areas when measured 10-69 years after the 1st vaccination.
claims.locator: Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing, 'Yellow fever', The Australian Immunisation Handbook, at https://immunisationhandbook.health.gov.au/contents/vaccine-preventable-diseases/yellow-fever, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Laboratory workers: 1 dose**, and **with ongoing exposure, measure neutralising antibody if the last dose was 10 or more years ago**.
claims.source_text: 1 dose of yellow fever vaccine is recommended for people who work in laboratories with the yellow fever virus. Laboratory workers with ongoing exposure to yellow fever virus should have their neutralising antibody titres measured if their last vaccine dose was 10 years ago or more.
claims.locator: Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing, 'Yellow fever', The Australian Immunisation Handbook, at https://immunisationhandbook.health.gov.au/contents/vaccine-preventable-diseases/yellow-fever, retrieved 2026-09-23
